recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR source follow-up is needed for FHIR-27545; future review of the impurity type should use FHIR-31860 as the controlling later issue.
issue_request: FHIR-27545 was a Published/Persuasive R5 BR&R request to add MedicinalProductDefinition.impurity, cardinality 0..*, referencing SubstanceDefinition, with a definition for drug product impurities as components other than the drug substance or excipients.
initial_application: Git commit 85fd3327b880055735fc2c5a09c7b6ea6ef71086 explicitly applied FHIR#27545 by adding MedicinalProductDefinition.impurity to the then-authoritative spreadsheet as Reference(SubstanceDefinition) with the requested cardinality and definition. The later source-format rework preserved the element in source/medicinalproductdefinition/structuredefinition-MedicinalProductDefinition.xml.
additional_context: BR&R 2020-07-28 minutes record discussion and approval of FHIR-27545 by 19-0-0. Later Published/Persuasive issue FHIR-31860 asked why impurity was not CodeableReference, and commits 52e5bc15a64e4321f32cc52bc2a82cbeee74024e and 8c81e0e3fcd3456e8ce5d7a7c8c78e4dfdcae2a6 changed the impurity type from Reference to CodeableReference while retaining targetProfile SubstanceDefinition. source/fhir.ini actively lists both MedicinalProductDefinition and SubstanceDefinition resources.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source/medicinalproductdefinition/structuredefinition-MedicinalProductDefinition.xml defines MedicinalProductDefinition.impurity as 0..*, includes the requested impurity definition, and uses CodeableReference with targetProfile http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/SubstanceDefinition plus the substance-code example binding. Reverting the type to Reference would conflict with the later FHIR-31860 decision.
